Never thought I'd really enjoy a roguelike as much as I dig Darkest Dungeon at this point.

The story is simple and blunt, your goal given right on without too much context about everything. And given the focus of the game is the gameplay and about dungeon exploring, this is perfectly fine.

The graphics and music has a dark atmosphere in general, enhancing the setting and giving it the right vibes for the gloomy and dark situations you're getting thrown in. The art style has its nice and recognizable way to make the trips into the dungeons and explore those a good experience overall.

Given the genre, it's a repetitive cycle of you preparing your characters for the next exploration trip, expand your options in town to make them stronger, make services cheaper, and giving you better odds at not running into misery. Many classes to pick and build your teams around, themed teams for specific dungeon types making things a bit easier within those. Given the amount of skills every class has, you can go with different approaches and builds for them, not being a one-way ticket to only get used as a tank but a tank also able to go into an offensive build if you like this approach more.

Dungeon exploration is a matter how many items you took with you and into what obstacles you'll run eventually. Dungeon designs randomized, some dungeons ending up with a more tedious room layout, some on the straight and simple progression. Resource management will decide how decent or not a trip will be, gathering items to sell or collect for town upgrades, making decisions what to keep and what to drop as the inventory isn't the biggest. Quest tasks vary from exploring the whole dungeon to find specific objects to interact or to collect, different sizes and difficulties for the dungeons existing.

Battles are in general RPG style, choosing the skills you want to use, having specific ranges or positions you have to be in to use those. Hit and dodge chances giving everything an RNG touch while turn order also not solely relying on one stat but also has some RNG to it included. Enemy variation is big enough to not feel like you run into the same enemies over and over while different areas have a focus on specific enemy types. Your characters will get stressed and once too stressed, things could go 180 and make a run more complicated. With how much RNG is included within passives, status effects, and many more, the runs you expect to be easy may still turn something into results not expected, making it fun despite you doing these runs constantly.

Difficulty for the game is to me in the mid-levels, some enemies being on the comfier side to deal with while some will give you some headaches. Bosses do something annoying and even nasty, learning about those things when encountering those. And given a character's death is permanent, you have to make the right decisions whether to continue or be safe and bail out of a dungeon before worse happens. The game plays a lot of mind games with you and your decisions, but I didn't feel anything was overly difficult to even unfair. You can adapt to situations and areas with the right setups so things will get easier if you know what you do.

What increased my experience by a lot is how much the modding scene has to offer for the game. I only knew a few skins for classes to exist which were the reason why I got mildly interested in DD in the beginning, but once I saw what options I have and what modders created over the last decade, I've found a lot of visual changes which made the game a feast for my eyes. New classes, skins for those, many ways to tweak your game and experience it with a new touch. Not to mention that you can tweak a few things by yourself rather easy once figuring out which files are for what. I've made a few changes to my NPCs myself, and will surely do more of that in the future.

Negatives about the game? The usual easy to learn, and hard to master mentality comes into play for sure. It took some hours to get a gist of how to operate my runs, what options I have to make them a bit comfier, and what can wreck you and what to look out for.
I personally felt that the passives you may get after a successful run more often than not went into the negatives, receiving more bad passives over good ones, but there's eventually a mod to balance that out a bit more. Not sure if it's intended like that but felt a bit more geared towards receiving some bad passives, but could just be me not having the best luck with those.
Expect to curse a lot when your 90%+ hit chances end up in missing enemies, or you getting smacked into dangerous levels out of nowhere which can be funny in a grim way~

I'm usually not much into roguelikes, but the combination of how I can tweak the game to my liking plus the bit I've seen and knew about the game got me into giving it a try. Which resulted in my little issue to pick from a very few roguelikes to play whenever time and mood allows it to now being settled into these dungeons. To me, there's no real finish to the game, a lot of things you can do and also add with the help of mods to have a reason to come back whenever you desire. And when on sale, it's just a few bucks which is a lot you get out for such little investment. I like my games with clear goals and beating them, but this game is now fully accepted by me to come back to and enjoy the game.

Here, a single battle can easily take 3-5 minutes due to SLOOOW actions and SLOOOOOOOOW animations for every single action.

I tried, I honestly tried. But no. It's not bad but certainly not elite and on balance I unfortunately have to not recommend it. It feels like a much worse 'Slay the Spire' minus the deck-building. After a while, it gets a bit repetitive and boring: the same passages, rewards and enemies... Yes you build up to fighting different bosses but there wasn't quite enough variety to keep me hooked - Slay the Spire manages this way better. 

I also feel like it isn't balanced correctly. The whole premise is that your decisions are permanent so your 'favourite heroes' die if you make a mistake - but at the same time you have a near infinite supply of new heroes who you don't even have to pay to recruit. As such, the stakes don't feel nearly as high the game suggests. Also, all the heroes are basically different skins of the same type of hero. If you boil down their abilities, they're all quite similar: all of them have some combination of healing, de-stealthing, multi-target attack and single-target attack. I've never built my roster and thought: wow I definitely need this type of hero in it... All in all, it's probably worth giving a go if discounted but certainly not at full price.

I love this game, I really do, but no matter how much love I pour into it, it does not make it any less broken. The beginning of the game is excellent: nice, steady progression, good challenge, gradual level ups. The transition from apprentice to veteran is tough but surmountable, and I was having a great time. And then you hit champion level. The characters levels cap at 6, along with their armor and attack capabilities, and if the monsters in the new area were just harder hitting and had more effects with their attacks, that would be fine. Instead, the balance is utterly ruined by massively buffing their dodge and crit rate. 

The game changes completely from a challenging but fair experience that requires planning, forethought, and skill, and turns into a lottery roll. You go into champion dungeons just crossing your fingers that you don't run into monsters with attacks that crit nearly every time, attacks that can and will OHKO multiple party members in one swing, and so on. And these are NOT bosses. These are random enemy encounters where a 75% chance to hit equates to missing five times in a row, then having the enemy critical hit multiple characters in one turn and deathblow them before you can even blink.

Now I know there are people out there that love this, and I'm glad there are because everyone deserves a game that hits just right for them. Unfairness is a genuine appeal to some players, and that's okay, but if that is not something that appeals to you, don't play this game. Don't sink hours into it only to get two thirds of the way in and be completely stonewalled by RNG.

I'm sure a lot of people would laugh at this review and say "if you don't like challenge, then this isn't the game for you" but in my opinion, challenge and RNG are complete opposites. Challenge is something that requires skill to overcome. There is no way to overcome RNG. There is no combat tactic that will stop a crit sweep. There is no prior planning that can mitigate losing your vital trinkets that you cannot ever get back. That's not challenge, and it's not fun for me. If I wanted to play an RNG game that I will always lose, I'd buy a lottery ticket. As for DD, I think I need to just uninstall it. At least I had some fun before it shot itself in the foot.

This may not be the best dungeon crawler, best roguelike, or best turn based games I've played.
However, this game has one of the best themes, and it sticks to it like glue.
The story, albeit simple, glued me to this game for my first 5-10 hours.

I now play it an hour a day, do a few runs, and move on. This game respects your time thats for sure.
Its hard, sometimes hair pulling hard, but not the hardest.
There is plenty of room to learn mechanics, counters, so on.

The game has flaws, all games do, but this game is just so catching.
Its one of my favourites, its soundtrack is godly, and its atmosphere is second to none. (also a good avenue into lovecraftian lore/horror)
The opening has lived rent free in my brain since I first seen it, and I unironically make quotes of the narrator when playing other games. 

Maybe do what I do and have this as a "secondary playthrough" game, where you take breaks from your main games to chip away a few dungeon runs into this one, I promise you the change of pace is a great palate cleanser.
That's specially the case if you are starting to feel burnt out of the potential grind, or just feel the need to take a break, Its very likely unique enough from whatever you are playing beside it.

All in all I think this game is amazing, I do not much care for its DLCs, most have been not the best: I either dislike them or have no opinion on them.
But this game, Darkest Dungeon, is amazing and worth the try. Either as your new game to be hooked on, or a new side hustle to chip away while you grind other games, either way its a great time.

I already had this game for PS Vita and I love it just as much on PC. Imagine a game that is a hybrid of turn based dungeon crawler RPG and sports team management sim. You constantly recruit and manage your team of adventurers, rotate them out and ensure their well being while they progress and develop both positive and negative traits. Death is permanent so ensuring that you have plenty of capable party members waiting in reserve is crucial. If you enjoy both adventuring as well as tweaking and managing stats this game is going to be right up your alley. You will find what archetypes complement each other and what strategies to build your different parties around. The game can be punishingly difficult at times (at least for me it was) and will test your resolve and management skills.

One of the best games I ever played. Very atmospheric. Every dungeon dive feels trepidious since there's permadeath, and the music and voiceover pulls you in. Limited inventory forces you to choose between supplies (safety) and loot (reward). There's no clear-cut choice. Because light and food dwindle over time the further you dungeon dive, it becomes a race to reach your objectives. And on top of all this, you need to manage your heroes' stress. Simply brilliant.
